title: Estrategias de marketing holístico para potenciar negocios digitales en Neiva, Turbo y Valledupar.
summary: Abstract This study aims to analyze how the implementation of holistic marketing strategies can boost digital businesses in three regions with growing economies: Neiva (Huila), Turbo (Antioquia), and Valledupar (Cesar). The study seeks to enhance the customer experience, competitiveness, and sustainability of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the retail and service sectors, which have made uneven progress in their digital transformation processes. The proposed methodology is based on a mixed-methods approach, combining surveys and interviews with business owners and customers in the three regions, along with an analysis of social media and digital platforms to identify current marketing practices. In addition, a case study will be conducted on companies in Neiva, Turbo, and Valledupar that have successfully integrated their physical and digital channels, with the aim of identifying patterns of success applicable to different regional contexts Expected results include the identification of effective holistic marketing strategies that contribute to local economic growth, strengthen customer loyalty, and optimize multichannel communication among SMEs in the three territories. Furthermore, the study aims to provide a reference model that guides businesses toward a sustainable digital transformation aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals. The expected results include the identification of effective holistic marketing strategies that contribute to local economic growth, strengthen customer loyalty, and optimize multichannel communication in SMEs across the three territories. title: Cargo-vessel Congestion at Three Major United States Gateways During the 2020–2022 Supply-chain Disruption
summary: The 2020–2022 disruption of global supply chains produced severe cargo-ship congestion at United States gateway ports, yet much of the public evidence rests on news reports and proprietary indices rather than open vessel-movement data. This study quantifies and compares cargo-vessel congestion at three major US gateways, Los Angeles/Long Beach, Houston/Galveston, and New York/New Jersey, using open Automatic Identification System (AIS) data from the United States Nationwide AIS archive. To capture within-year variation while controlling for season, two reference months, January and July, were analysed for each of 2020, 2021, and 2022; the analysis therefore rests on selected monthly snapshots rather than a continuous series. Daily indicators of waiting vessels, formally anchored vessels, anchorage dwell time, and throughput were derived, with uncertainty quantified by an autocorrelation-aware moving block bootstrap and robustness confirmed by threshold sensitivity analyses. The congestion signal is strong and spatially uneven. At Los Angeles/Long Beach the mean number of waiting cargo vessels rose from 29 per day in early 2020 to a peak near 69 per day in mid-2021 and remained close to that level into January 2022 before easing to 51 by July 2022; New York/New Jersey stayed comparatively low throughout, and Houston/Galveston surged latest, peaking in mid-2022. All principal contrasts remain significant under the block bootstrap. At Los Angeles/Long Beach waiting grew far faster than throughput (134% versus 23% from January 2020 to 2022), indicating demand exceeding berth capacity rather than merely higher arrivals, and a divergence between formal anchoring and broader waiting is consistent with the offshore queuing system introduced in November 2021. The within-area counts, which the authoritative Marine Exchange of Southern California series tracks, are conservative because part of the queue lay offshore of the study area. Within the limits of its selected-month design, the study is a reproducible comparative assessment rather than a continuous reconstruction of the disruption.

title: Research on Optimization Strategies for Reverse Supply Chains of Port Waste Materials and Containers from the Circular Economy Perspective
summary: With the continuous expansion of global shipping volume and accelerating green low-carbon transition of ports, establishing reverse supply chains for waste materials represents a core pathway for ports to implement the 3R principles of circular economy. Domestic ports in China are currently confronted with prevalent challenges, including fragmented recycling systems, extensive sorting and disposal practices, broken resource recycling links, and insufficient coordination mechanisms among multiple stakeholders, which greatly hinder sustainable port development. This paper reviews reverse governance practices at domestic and international ports such as Ningbo Zhoushan Port, Shanghai Yangshan Port, Port of Singapore and Port of Rotterdam, and identifies replicable experiences including centralized collection, intelligent sorting, full life cycle closed-loop operation and multi-party collaborative governance. It is noted that existing practices mostly focus on fragmented improvements targeting isolated individual links. Drawing on circular economy theories, this paper integrates strengths from multiple case studies and proposes an integrated optimization system for reverse supply chains characterized by “unified network-based collection, two-tier classification, three stage closed-loop circulation and four dimensional co-governance”. A multi-dimensional governance platform integrating multi-stakeholder collaboration, digital traceability and institutional constraints is further constructed to cut operational costs of reverse logistics. This research provides theoretical support and practical solutions for the green transformation and upgrading of reverse supply chains for port waste materials and containers.

title: Used Cooking Oil Supply Chain Risk Management (Used Cooking Oil) Based on ISO 31000:2018
summary: Indonesia's reliance on fossil fuels and the growing volume of household used cooking oil (UCO) present opportunities for a sustainable biodiesel business while simultaneously introducing complex risks across the supply chain. This article outlines and analyzes the risk management plan of PT Biofuel Unggul Lestari (PT BUL)—a company engaged in the collection, pre-treatment, and export of UCO—based on the ISO 31000:2018 Risk Management Guidelines framework. This descriptive-qualitative study employs a case study approach, using External Factor Evaluation (EFE) and Internal Factor Evaluation (IFE) analyzes as the basis for risk identification, alongside the Risk Priority Number (RPN = Probability × Impact, on a scale of 1–5) method to assess and prioritize risks. The identification process revealed 35 risks categorized as either internal or external: 18 were classified as High, 17 as Medium, and none as Critical. The five risks with the highest RPN scores (16) were fluctuations in the Crude Palm Oil (CPO) reference price, reliance on a single supplier, exchange rate risk, sudden changes in government regulations, and competition from CPO-based rivals and regional players. Mitigation strategies implemented include a combination of risk reduction and transfer measures, such as supplier diversification based on the 20:80 principle, long-term supply contracts, hedging via forward contracts, and accelerating International Sustainability and Carbon Certification (ISCC) acquisition. These findings confirm that the application of systematic, international-standard risk management can serve as a foundation for the sustainability of waste-based biodiesel businesses in Indonesia.

title: The Impact of AI Token Trading Replacing Traditional Currency in AI Technology Enterprises on Corporate Performance
summary: The intangible, instantly delivered, and continuously consumed nature of AI compute services exposes three inherent frictions in fiat-based settlement: temporal mismatches, coarse pricing granularity, and cross-border delays. This study investigates whether AI-Token—the atomic unit of model inference and training—can serve as a more efficient medium of exchange than fiat currency in B2B AI transactions, and how such a shift affects firm performance. Integrating transaction cost economics, agency theory, and corporate finance, it constructs a three-layer framework that traces how Token's roles as a means of payment, cost item, and asset class generate distinct causal pathways to revenue-side, cost-side, and asset-side performance. Employing theoretical synthesis and deductive analysis, this paper provides a unified conceptual architecture for future empirical research on programmable settlement media in the digital economy.

title: Asset Classification as a Hidden Liability: Carbon Accounting and Corporate Valuation Bias in China's ETS
summary: Despite the rapid growth of carbon markets, accounting standards remain silent on whether emission allowances should be classified as intangible assets or financial instruments. China's prevailing requirement to record allowances as intangible assets at historical cost prevents balance sheets from reflecting market prices, systematically biasing equity valuation downward. Using a comparative case design featuring leading power and steel producers, combined with valuation-model decomposition, this study demonstrates how the intangible-asset classification inflates price-to-book ratios and disrupts the logic of the EV/EBITDA framework. Research shows that introducing a dual classification model based on management intent—distinguishing between self-use and trading carbon emission rights and using historical cost and fair value measurement, respectively—can significantly improve the relevance of accounting information. Based on this, the paper proposes policy recommendations to revise accounting standards, adjust valuation models, and strengthen carbon finance regulation, aiming to improve the quality of carbon accounting information, help the capital market accurately price green assets, and promote high-quality economic development under the "dual carbon" goal.

title: Research on the Transformation Path of China's New Energy Vehicle Industry Entering the European Market in the Digital Age
summary: The extension of China's new energy vehicles to Europe has gained momentum in recent years; but the tough regulatory environment and the high level of development in the systems of automobile industries in Europe have necessitated the transformation of traditional export patterns. Not much literature has been devoted to examining the necessary strategy adjustments for Chinese new energy vehicles in terms of changes in internationalization modes and competitive dynamics in Europe. This paper is based on theories related to the Eclectic Paradigm of International Production (OLI) and dynamic capabilities, using data from industries, government documents, and case studies at the firm level to investigate the effect of digital transformation on Chinese new energy vehicles' expansion and competitive advantage formation in Europe. The research findings indicate that Chinese new energy vehicles at present depend on battery technology, economies of scale, and their supply chain advantages for expansion in Europe; but traditional export patterns cannot help sustain in the long run. Digital transformation enhances data utilization, software capabilities, and user engagement capabilities, enabling firms to convert manufacturing advantages into digital competitive advantages and to drive their transition from product exports to digital-enabled localized operations. At the same time, European green regulations and data governance requirements further push firms to enhance their digital supply chain management and compliance capabilities

title: Digitisation of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Reporting in Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (SMES): Quality of Information and Implications for Portugal
summary: This article examines the digitalisation of non-financial reporting and Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) reporting in Europe, with a particular focus on small and medium-sized enterprises and the implications for Portugal. Through a structured narrative review of recent scientific literature and regulatory and technical documentation, the study analyses how digital infrastructures, regulatory frameworks, and organisational conditions affect the quality of the information disclosed. The analysis is organised around six key areas: regulatory developments in reporting, information quality, the role of eXtensible Business Reporting Language (XBRL) and the European Single Electronic Format (ESEF), the tension between standardisation and flexibility, implementation constraints in SMEs, and the importance of data governance. The results show that digitisation can improve the traceability, comparability, analytical reusability, and verifiability of reporting, but these effects are not automatic. Their realisation depends on semantic consistency, tagging discipline, internal validation, technical capabilities, and institutional support. Furthermore, the review suggests that SMEs face the greatest challenges in this transition, due to constraints in terms of resources, training, tools, and data collection. For Portugal, the study concludes that improving digital reporting requires regulatory proportionality, institutional mediation, and operational frameworks that strengthen internal management capacity.

title: Digital transformation in healthcare sector: The current state of hospitals in Nigeria and care homes in the United Kingdom
summary: Digital transformation is increasingly central to healthcare and social care delivery, yet its uptake remains uneven across contexts. This article compares the current state of digital transformation in private hospitals in Nigeria and care homes in the United Kingdom using a qualitative comparative case study (n = 15) and thematic analysis. Cross-case synthesis using a comparative matrix highlights both shared conditions (documentation intensity and regulatory scrutiny) and structural differences (infrastructure reliability, financing, and ecosystem integration). The findings indicate that digital maturity is shaped more by location and contextual readiness than by leaders’ tenure, and that adoption is commonly incremental and compliance-led. Key barriers include digital capability gaps and infrastructural constraints, while digitally confident younger managers often act as implementation champions. By mapping themes to transformational leadership, Kotter’s change model and diffusion stages, the article develops an inductively derived conceptual framework explaining triggers, enabling conditions and embedding dynamics in regulated care organizations.

title: Driving Sustainable Innovation through Digital Transformation: A Behavioural Model of the Upcycling Craft Industry in Indonesia
summary: Background Digital transformation has emerged as a key driver of competitiveness across industries, yet its adoption in the upcycling craft sector remains insufficiently explored. Existing studies often focus on large enterprises, leaving a research gap in understanding how micro-scale, resource-constrained upcycling businesses integrate digital technologies, specifically within the Indonesian upcycling craft sector context. This study addresses this gap by developing the Behavioral-Based Digital Transformation (BBDT) model to investigate behavioral determinants of digital adoption, implementation, and innovation outcomes in Indonesia’s sustainability-oriented creative sector. Method This study employed a sequential exploratory mixed-methods approach. The qualitative phase involved field observations and in-depth interviews with three upcycling craft enterprises, while the quantitative phase surveyed 30 micro-scale upcycling businesses across multiple Indonesian regions. Data were analyzed using thematic coding, NVivo software, and Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to test the proposed Behavioral-Based Digital Transformation (BBDT) model. Results and Conclusion Findings indicate that internal and external factors, including leadership commitment, financial capability, and market demand, significantly shape behavioral orientation toward digital adoption. Behavioral intentions, in turn, drive digital technology implementation, enhancing operational efficiency, material optimization, and product innovation. Digital adoption acts as both an outcome and enabler of early-stage sustainable transformation pathways, sustainable transformation, with innovation reinforcing initial cycles of engagement with technology. The study provides preliminary support for the mediating role of behavioral intention and underscores the critical importance of human and organizational readiness. These insights offer theoretical contributions to TAM, TPB, and IDT integration and practical guidance for policymakers, creative communities, and micro-enterprise owners.

title: Criminal Liability for the Manipulation of Financial Statements from the Perspective of Government Regulation Number 43 of 2025 Concerning Financial Reporting
summary: This study, entitled "Corporate Criminal Liability for Financial Statement Manipulation from the Perspective of Government Regulation Number 43 of 2025 concerning Financial Reporting," examines corporate financial statement manipulation (case studies of PT Garuda Indonesia Tbk and PT Hanson International Tbk) alongside the implications of Government Regulation (PP) No. 43 of 2025. It aims to analyze the imposition of sanctions on corporations engaging in financial statement manipulation and examine the role of PP No. 43 of 2025 as a mitigation tool for financial reporting crimes. Using a normative legal method with a descriptive-analytical specification, secondary data were collected through library research and analyzed normatively-qualitatively. The results show that corporate criminal liability is applied when intentionality (mens rea) in presenting false and misleading information is proven, rather than mere technical accounting errors. PP No. 43 of 2025 functions as a preventive and evidential mitigation instrument through reporting standardization, preparer competency requirements, mandatory liability statements, and the integration of the Joint Financial Reporting Platform (PBPK), which strengthens the chain of accountability and digital evidence for criminal law enforcement.

title: Digital transformation of land resource management in ukraine: from geographic information systems to intelligent agents
summary: The article examines the evolution of digital tools for land resource management in Ukraine through the lens of changing technological paradigms. Three successive generations of digital solutions are distinguished: the first, based on geographic information systems and digital soil mapping; the second, on machine-learning methods and the digital-twin concept; and the third, on generative artificial intelligence and large-language-model (LLM) agents. The study analyses the state of the national regulatory framework, data infrastructure and human capacity in the land-cadastre domain. It is shown that the transition to the third generation is not merely a quantitative improvement of individual indicators but a qualitative redefinition of the human role in spatial analysis: the analyst shifts from operator to task-setter, while the agent autonomously plans and performs the analytical process. Using a unified set of parameters, a comparative characterisation of the three generations is compiled, and a matrix of barriers and opportunities is formed across five domains — data, human capacity, regulation, financing and security. Key prerequisites for a technological-leapfrogging trajectory are substantiated in the context of post-war reconstruction and European integration, together with the imperative of a human-in-the-loop principle for legally significant cadastral data.Received: 08.06.2026;Accepted: 22.06.2026;

title: Transformational and Inclusive Leadership Communication in Driving Public Sector Organizational Change in the Digital Transformation Era
summary: This research examines the role of transformational leadership communication mechanisms in driving public sector organizational change in the digital transformation era, with a case study at the Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Indonesia thru the "Kemenkeu Satu" application. A qualitative approach with a single case study design was used, focusing on the analysis of publicly documented leadership communication practices. Data was collected from secondary documents, such as leadership speeches and statements, news releases, official press releases, and public policy documents containing narratives of organizational integration, work values, and digital transformation agendas. Data analysis was conducted using thematic coding techniques to identify communication patterns that reflect the dimensions of transformational leadership and the strengthening of an inclusive climate. The research findings indicate that leadership communication serves as a managerial mechanism that unifies the direction of change, strengthens the legitimacy of the transformation, and manages the organization's internal diversity. The "Kemenkeu Satu" program is positioned as an integrative narrative that connects the vision of change, the value of integrity, cross-unit collaboration, and the drive for digital-based learning and innovation. This finding confirms that the success of public organizational transformation is not solely determined by formal policies and structures, but also by the consistency and quality of leadership communication in building shared meaning and workplace cultural cohesion. Practically, this research shows that change management in public organizations requires a consistent, inclusive, and continuous learning-oriented leadership communication strategy for digital transformation to be effective. This research enriches the public sector change management literature with thematic evidence on how leadership communication manages internal diversity to strengthen cultural cohesion and commitment to change. However, this study has some limitations, including reliance on secondary data which may limit direct understanding of individual contexts within the organization and potential interpretive bias from available documents.

title: Addressing Performance Gaps in Kenya's Public Benefit Organizations: The Role of Communication Strategies and Digital Transformation
summary: Public Benefit Organizations (PBOs) in Kenya play a crucial role in socio-economic development, contributing 2.2% of GDP in 2023 and over 325,000 jobs. These organizations provide critical services in various sectors helping to fill the voids created by the government and private institutions. Reduced funding, poor compliance, inefficiencies in the use of resources and weak governance systems have resulted in numerous closings and deregistration of 2,802 PBOs between 2023 and 2024. Funding utilization stands at less than 55% with only 61% of registered PBOs filling their annual reports in 2023. The reliance on donations makes organizations volatile and mission-misaligned, while lack of digital maturity hinders modernization, with only 30% of organizations integrating technology in their operations in 2025. These constraints make PBOs vulnerable to organizational failures that result in deregistration, loss of jobs, inefficiency, and lack of sustainability. To address these gaps, the role of Communication Strategies as a change management strategy and Digital Transformation on the performance of PBOs in Kenya is at the center of this study. Anchored on Dynamic Capabilities Theory and the Resource Based View (RBV), this research utilized a pragmatic mixed method approach. A descriptive cross-sectional survey was conducted targeting 4,750 compliant PBOs. Using stratified random, a sample of 368 PBOs was drawn out of whom 261 returned usable questionnaires (response rate of 71%). Reliability was established (Cronbach’s α>0.70), construct validity was confirmed from factor analysis, and statistical tests included chi-square test, regression and path analyses, alongside thematic analysis of qualitative data. Results showed that communication strategies (β = -0.046, p=0.818) alone had no statistical significance, indicating poor institutionalization and constraints such as poor coordination and lack of feedback among others. Digital transformation was found to be a direct determinant (β = 0.495, p = 0.017) and moderator (β = 1.598, p = 0.004) of communication strategies impact. Results of qualitative research substantiated these findings, where the respondents pointed out that there was opposition to the process of change regarding new communication techniques, and feedback loops were found to be poor. Transparency and clarity were seen as success elements, but their implementation was difficult in practice. Challenges associated with technology adoption with digital transformation are required as part of the organization’s culture rather than just an add-on. The research makes contributions to dynamic capabilities theory for the non-profit organizations, by improving participatory governance and communication frameworks, and by contributing to digital transformation in the resource constrained environments. By bridging global theories with empirical evidence from Kenya’s nonprofit sector, the research provides actionable insights for policymakers and practitioners seeking to foster innovation, alignment, and resilience in dynamic environments.

title: Modeling the dynamics of digital transformation in social enterprises using an ISM-MICMAC approach in the GCC region
summary: Abstract This research investigates the organizational-level enabling and challenging factors affecting the digital transformation of social enterprises in the Kingdom of Bahrain and the State of Kuwait, two member states of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), highlighting the importance of digital technologies in enhancing operational efficiency, social impact, and sustainability within the sector. Employing a qualitative methodology, this study conducts semi-structured interviews with 20 managers and top employees from various social enterprises across both countries. Thematic analysis of the interview data shows 26 factors that influence the digital transformation of social enterprises. Furthermore, 12 professional experts from different sectors engaged in a Delphi analysis and identified the 14 most influential factors that impact the digital transformation of social enterprises. Using the Interpretive Structural Modeling (ISM) technique, the research uniquely constructs hierarchical relationships among the most influential factors influencing the digital transformation. Four drivers were identified in the ISM hierarchy: technology readiness, strategic vision & planning, digital and adaptive leadership, and collaborative ecosystem. The research also employs Cross-Impact Matrix Multiplication Applied to Classification (MICMAC) analysis to segregate these factors into four quadrants: Autonomous, Independent, Linkage and Dependent. This research creates a conceptual framework that guides social enterprises in implementing effective digital transformation strategies. It ultimately provides actionable recommendations for stakeholders to enhance their digital capabilities and increase social impact.

title: Branding the green games: discursive power and communicative inequality in Olympic sponsorship narratives
summary: Purpose This study aims to investigate how Olympic TOP sponsors construct green narratives across corporate, media and social media platforms and how these narratives contribute to communicative inequality in global environmental discourse. It explores the symbolic and rhetorical strategies used to project sustainability and interrogates the power structures that enable certain actors to dominate environmental meaning-making in the Olympic context. Design/methodology/approach This research uses a qualitative multimethod approach combining critical discourse analysis and qualitative content analysis. It analyses data from 10 Olympic TOP sponsors across environmental, social and governance (ESG) reports, news media and social media related to the Tokyo 2020, Beijing 2022 and Paris 2024 Olympic cycles, with focused data collection conducted between March 2023 and August 2024. Findings This study identifies three dominant greenwashing strategies – symbolic commitment, technological deflection and corporate social responsibility (CSR) performance theatre – varying across sectors. It highlights discursive patterns such as future deferral, selective framing and omission of dissent. Results show that corporate sponsors leverage symbolic alignment with the Olympics to shape sustainability discourse while excluding independent verification and marginalised voices, reinforcing communicative inequality. Originality/value This research reframes greenwashing as a systemic discursive phenomenon embedded in symbolic and institutional power, rather than isolated deception. It introduces “communicative inequality” as a critical lens for examining ESG narratives and offers a new framework for analysing sustainability discourse in mega-event sponsorships. This study contributes to both environmental communication and CSR literature by highlighting the politics of visibility, voice and legitimacy in corporate green storytelling.

title: Neurosymbolic code auditing
summary: Code auditing examines whether an implementation satisfies target properties such as reliability, security, performance, and design intent. Classical static analysis provides rigorous foundations for automated auditing, but it remains difficult to apply broadly in real-world software. The emergence of large language models (LLMs) and agents creates new opportunities for leveraging semantic cues that are embedded in source code, documentation, and other software artifacts yet difficult for classical static analyzers to derive. This survey presents a comprehensive study of neurosymbolic code auditing, an emerging synthesis that integrates LLM-driven reasoning with classical static analysis and other structured program reasoning techniques. By formalizing the cognitive processes underlying manual code auditing, this study conceptualizes an agent-centric framework that serves as a unifying foundation for neurosymbolic analysis. Specifically, this study categorizes LLM-enabled primitive analyses over both code and non-code artifacts, addressing the fundamental reasoning tasks routinely performed by human auditors. Furthermore, the authors review a broad spectrum of neurosymbolic architectures that combine symbolic tools with LLM-based reasoning, illustrating how these systems replicate and extend the practical strategies employed by human auditors. Lastly, the authors synthesize the survey around three recurring bottlenecks, namely, observation, verification and memory, then outline future directions and the persistent technical challenges.

title: Climate change exposure and firm value in China: evidence consistent with a discount-rate interpretation
summary: This paper examines the relationship between firm-level climate change exposure and firm value in China. Using A-share listed firms from 2002 to 2020 and a disclosure-based measure of perceived climate change exposure, we find a significant negative association between climate change exposure and firm value. Our measure provides incremental explanatory power beyond conventional proxies, including ESG indicators and climate change news risk measures. Channel tests provide evidence consistent with a discount-rate interpretation. Both transition and physical-risk exposures are negatively associated with firm value. However, for firms in carbon-neutral industries, transition exposure is positively associated with firm value, consistent with transition-related growth opportunities. The negative associations are more pronounced for firms in high-pollution industries and coastal regions. Further results indicate that the negative valuation association is weaker among firms with stronger green innovation and ESG ratings. Overall, our findings highlight the pricing of climate risk and the role of transition opportunities in firm valuation.

title: A Review of the Impact of ESG Performance on Investment Portfolio Performance
summary: The relationship between ESG performance and investment portfolio performance has become a focal point of academic debate. This review systematically examines studies from 2009 to 2024 indexed in Web of Science, Scopus, and CNKI databases, organizing them around three interrelated questions: does ESG integration help or hurt returns, by what mechanisms does it operate, and why do empirical findings differ so sharply across studies? Three broad positions emerge. The positive school argues that ESG leadership builds intangible capital—stakeholder trust, and reputational resilience—that conventional financial metrics tend to miss. The negative school contends that ESG constraints narrow the investment universe and suppress expected returns. A third, more skeptical position holds that the divergence in findings is largely an artifact of inconsistent rating methodologies and sample choices rather than evidence for or against ESG per se. Empirical data from MSCI indices over 2016–2025 show ESG-screened portfolios performing on par with conventional benchmarks, with compound annual growth rates of 12.17% for both. The review finds that ESG integration is most reliably associated with reduced tail-risk exposure and lower financing costs, rather than with systematic outperformance. Whether it improves risk-adjusted returns depends heavily on which rating agency's scores are used, the market in question, and how the portfolio is constructed.

title: Risk Propagation and Resilience Early Warning in Manufacturing Supply Chains Under Generative AI–Driven Public-Opinion Disturbances
summary: INTRODUCTION: To address three challenges arising from the large-scale generation and cross-platform dissemination of generative AI content—namely, the difficulty of quantifying external information disturbances in manufacturing supply chains, time-varying risk-propagation relationships, and the limited credibility of early warnings—we propose a Generative-AI-Aware Risk Transmission and Resilience Prediction Network GAI-RTPNet. OBJECTIVES: The network constructs a node-level exogenous disturbance representation from semantic polarity, event relevance, propagation intensity, source credibility, content novelty, AI-generation probability, and semantic consistency. It updates the edge weights of supply relationships through disturbance-driven dynamic graph attention and jointly models risk evolution across nodes and time periods using a risk-propagation gate and temporal self-attention. METHODS: Based on a shared spatiotemporal representation, GAI-RTPNet applies multitask learning to simultaneously predict future node risk, propagation probabilities, and system resilience. It further combines heteroscedastic and model uncertainty estimates to produce four-tier trustworthy early warnings. RESULTS: Experiments on GDELT 2.0, SupplyGraph, and HC3 show that GAI-RTPNet achieves values of 0.048, 0.867, and 0.041 for Risk MAE, Propagation Accuracy, and Resilience MAE, respectively, with a mean warning lead time of 4.1 d. Its performance remains stable under noise, random missingness, and cross-scenario testing. CONCLUSION: The results support the effectiveness of explicitly incorporating generative-AI-driven public-opinion disturbances into dynamic-graph risk propagation and resilience prediction, providing a unified data-driven approach to risk identification, risk-propagation inference, and proactive warning in manufacturing supply chains.

title: An integrated decision-making framework for modelling key drivers and barriers to sustainable supply chain adoption in the textile manufacturing industry
summary: Sustainable supply chain management (SSCM) is vital for the textile industry in emerging economies like Bangladesh, where environmental compliance, global buyer pressure, and resource constraints intersect. Yet, translating sustainability commitments into effective SSCM practices remains challenging in textile supply chains in emerging economies such as Bangladesh. Existing studies have often examined SSCM drivers and barriers separately, with limited integration of hierarchical driver analysis, causal barrier assessment, and scenario-sensitive prioritization within a unified decision-making framework. Examining both dimensions is essential because drivers represent enabling conditions for SSCM adoption, whereas barriers constrain their effective implementation. This study, therefore, identifies and evaluates key drivers and barriers to SSCM through a structured literature review and expert validation involving 67 experts in the validation phase and 56 experts in the model-development phase. This study integrates modified Total Interpretive Structural Modelling (m-TISM), Matrix Cross-Reference Multiplication Applied to a Classification (MICMAC) analysis, fuzzy Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (DEMATEL), and Graph Theory with Matrix Approach (GTMA) to assess hierarchical driver-barrier structures, interrelationships, and network-sensitive barrier prioritization. Findings reveal technological readiness, reverse logistics, and regulatory enforcement as primary drivers, while financial constraints, infrastructure gaps, and weak enforcement are key barriers varying significantly across firm-size scenarios. The study's novelty lies in integrating hierarchical driver modelling, causal barrier analysis, and scenario-sensitive network prioritization to guide scale-sensitive SSCM interventions in the textile supply chains in the emerging economies.

title: The Green Investment Paradox in Japan: Growth, Energy, and Financial Realities
summary: This study examines the concept of "green finance," a cornerstone of sustainable development, in the context of the Japanese economy, exploring its empirical and theoretical dimensions. The relationship between renewable energy consumption (RENE), GDP per capita, and foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows was econometrically tested using data from Japan for the period 1990-2024. ADF unit root tests applied within the econometric analysis framework showed that the variables were not stationary at their level values but became stationary (I(1)) after taking their first differences. The results of the "Bootstrap ARDL Bound Test" applied subsequently confirmed the existence of a long-term cointegration relationship between the variables. Japan has announced its Green Growth Strategy in line with its goal of becoming carbon neutral by 2050, and has become the second-largest green bond issuer in Asia. However, the analysis reveals that there are still significant gaps between goals and practices. Specifically, the increasing dependence on fossil fuels after nuclear energy, the slowness in investment and implementation processes, and the risks of "greenwashing" in ESG investments have been identified as the main challenges. title: Mapping ESG evolution in Brazilian ports: A text-mining approach to sustainability reporting
summary: The alignment of port sustainability governance with international maritime policy frameworks requires ports to move beyond compliance-oriented reporting towards substantive climate performance disclosure. This study investigates the evolution of ESG disclosures in Brazilian ports and terminals over 2018-2024, examining whether reporting patterns reflect substantive sustainability integration or legitimacy-oriented discursive alignment. A text-mining approach is applied to 87 sustainability reports issued by the 16 throughput-dominant operators that jointly account for 76.6% of Brazil's cargo throughput. An open mapping analysis extracts the 100 most frequent terms per year and visualises co-occurrence networks using Python and VOSviewer. A controlled vocabulary of 398 search expressions, constructed from established public reference frameworks, validated through independent double coding (Cohen's kappa = 0.88) and corroborated by Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic modelling, measures term frequencies across five ESG dimensions: governance; operational efficiency and safety; climate change and energy transition; social responsibility and stakeholder engagement; and port–city and environmental interface. The findings reveal persistent dominance of governance and Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) compliance vocabulary, while climate-related language remains structurally marginal, a pattern consistent with legitimacy-oriented disclosure and mimetic isomorphism under neo-institutional theory and robust to conglomerate reports, network thresholds and the public-private split. Two findings sharpen the picture: disclosure intensity shows only a weak and statistically non-significant association with port size, indicating that Brazil's largest throughput-dominant operators are not necessarily its climate-reporting leaders; and the governance-over-climate imbalance is widest among public port authorities, precisely where public accountability is greatest. This misalignment with the International Maritime Organization's (IMO) 2050 decarbonisation pathway matters for maritime regulators, and the validated five-cluster taxonomy offers a replicable benchmarking instrument for emerging-economy port systems.

title: Digital Transformation as an Organisational Change Process in Higher Education: A Qualitative Research at a Large Public University in Poland
summary: Digital transformation in higher education requires not only technology adoption but also effective organisational change management. While existing research has examined institutional strategies and technological infrastructure, limited attention has been paid to how system users perceive digitalisation during early implementation stages – a critical phase when resistance and uncertainty are most likely to emerge. This study addresses that gap by exploring user perceptions of digital transformation through the lens of change management theory. The research was conducted at a large public university in Poland undergoing digitalisation of administrative processes. An exploratory qualitative approach was adopted, involving four semi-structured interviews with administrative system users. The findings indicate that digital systems are generally perceived as beneficial for operational efficiency, but they also reveal challenges related to insufficient communication, unclear procedures, and inadequate preparation for change. These early-stage results highlight the importance of human-centered change strategies while ensuring alignment between technological implementation, organisational practices, and user competencies.

title: Grid-based environmental governance and the energy transition of rural households: evidence from the China labor-force dynamics survey
summary: Introduction We examine whether grid-based environmental governance promotes clean cooking fuel use among rural households through local grassroots governance and public service delivery. Methods We exploit the staggered rollout across Chinese cities as a natural experiment and link policy timing to rural household panel data from the China Labor-force Dynamics Survey covering 2012 to 2018. A multi-period difference-in-differences design identifies the policy effect. Results The policy significantly increases clean cooking fuel adoption. The mechanism estimates suggest three main channels: wider social security coverage, greater participation in public affairs, and higher household income. Effects are stronger in areas with weaker digital infrastructure, higher levels of human capital or urbanization, and among households with younger heads. Discussion Embedding environmental duties in local information collection, case referral, and public service networks allows the policy to ease information and service constraints during rural household energy transition. The findings suggest that stronger grassroots environmental governance can promote clean energy use across rural areas.

title: Green Computing Infrastructure and the Environmental Governance of Nearby Firms: Evidence from China’s National Green Data Centre Pilot
summary: Data centres are among the fastest-growing sources of electricity demand, and the policies that govern them are evaluated almost entirely by what happens inside the facility. This study asks whether such a policy also reaches the firms around it. Using 30,547 firm-year observations for 3918 Chinese A-share listed companies in 249 cities between 2010 and 2024, we treat successive designations under China’s National Green Data Center Pilot as a staggered, city-level shock and estimate its effect on how firms govern environmental responsibility. Governance is measured as the balance of favourable and adverse environmental events recorded for a firm by regulators, certifiers and complainants, rather than by what the firm says about itself. Designation shifts that balance towards the favourable side by roughly an eighth of a standard deviation. Decomposing the record locates the movement: firms become markedly more likely to hold a favourable environmental record and markedly less likely to hold none at all, while adverse records, which are rare, move little. The finding survives cohort-robust estimators, randomisation inference, province-by-year fixed effects, three alternative designation dates, and a rank-based recoding that removes the index’s ceiling. The governance return is larger where the local knowledge base is deeper and smaller where same-industry firms are densely clustered, indicating that local absorptive capacity, not the infrastructure alone, governs the return. Estimates are positive across eastern and non-eastern, coastal and inland, state-owned and private, and manufacturing and non-manufacturing firms. Green digital infrastructure therefore delivers sustainability value well beyond its own energy footprint.

title: Assessing Blackboard LMS Implementation, Adoption Barriers and Digital Transformation in Tertiary Institutions in Kogi State, Nigeria
summary: The adoption of digital learning technologies has intensified the need for evidence-based evaluation of Learning Management System (LMS) interventions in developing-country tertiary institutions. Despite substantial investment in digital infrastructure through the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund), empirical evidence on the implementation and utilization of TETFund sponsored Blackboard LMS in tertiary institutions in Kogi State, Nigeria, remains limited. This study evaluated Blackboard LMS implementation and utilization, examined factors influencing adoption, identified implementation challenges, and assessed strategies for improving effective use. A descriptive survey design was adopted involving lecturers from six tertiary institutions in Kogi State. Data were collected from 164 valid respondents using a structured four-section questionnaire and analysed using frequencies, percentages, means, and grand means, with a criterion mean of 2.50. Findings revealed low Blackboard LMS implementation and utilization, with a grand mean of 2.14, indicating limited integration into teaching, learning, and assessment activities. Although management support (M = 2.58), staff training (M = 2.55), and ICT infrastructure (M = 2.58) received positive ratings, the overall adoption-factor mean remained below the criterion level (M = 2.38), reflecting inadequate internet connectivity (M = 2.08) and network availability (M = 2.11). Major barriers included frequent power outages (M = 3.45), poor internet connectivity (M = 3.30), high internet subscription costs (M = 3.14), limited device access (M = 3.12), inadequate LMS awareness (M = 3.06), and insufficient ICT competence (M = 2.90). The study concludes that LMS availability alone does not ensure meaningful digital transformation; effective implementation requires reliable connectivity, sustainable power, continuous capacity development, institutional policy support, technical assistance, and systematic monitoring. The findings provide context-specific evidence for strengthening TETFund sponsored digital learning interventions in Nigerian tertiary education.

summary: This is an accepted article with a DOI pre-assigned that is not yet published.This study investigates the “double bind” faced by female leaders in Indonesia’s healthcare sector—an emerging market characterized by high masculinity, patriarchal norms, and a two-tier system. We examine how female commissioners and female directors influence firm performance and whether corporate governance mechanisms (such as audit committees, institutional ownership, and managerial ownership) mitigate the performance effects of gender incongruity. We used a sequential method, starting with archival research and then a focus group discussion. Using a panel of 214 firm-year observations from all listed healthcare companies on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (2015–2024), we apply random-effects regression models to test direct and moderated relationships. The findings indicate that female commissioners and female directors are associated with significantly lower ROA, but this effect is attenuated by audit committees and institutional ownership. Our study thus extends the archival research results by identifying the factors that explain the process of female leadership.
